title: Understanding laboratory results
content: Use the reference range and measurement units printed by the testing laboratory. A result outside that range does not by itself establish a diagnosis, and a result inside it does not guarantee good health. Interpretation also depends on symptoms, history and other tests.

title: Blood glucose test
content: A blood glucose test measures sugar in a blood sample. Glucose results are used in diabetes assessment and monitoring. Fasting status and the type of test affect how a clinician interprets the measurement; an isolated result should be discussed in its clinical context.

title: Hemoglobin A1c test
content: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over approximately the preceding three months. It is used in diabetes assessment and monitoring. Some blood disorders and other conditions can affect its accuracy; personal treatment targets require clinical context.

title: Creatinine test
content: Creatinine is a waste product that kidneys remove from blood. Creatinine testing helps assess kidney function and may be used to estimate filtration. A result needs interpretation with other clinical information and cannot establish a kidney diagnosis on its own.

title: Complete blood count
content: A complete blood count measures blood cells and related characteristics, including hemoglobin, hematocrit and cell size. These tests support assessment of blood-related conditions. Abnormal counts have several possible explanations; history, symptoms and sometimes additional tests are needed.

title: Cholesterol levels
content: A cholesterol or lipid panel measures blood fats, including cholesterol and triglycerides. These results contribute to cardiovascular risk assessment. Interpretation and personal targets depend on the wider risk profile and medical history.

title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone test
content: TSH is a hormone involved in regulating thyroid activity. A TSH measurement helps assess thyroid function. Other thyroid tests and clinical information may be needed to understand an abnormal result.

title: Liver function tests
content: Liver test panels measure substances including enzymes, bilirubin and proteins. The pattern of results helps assess liver-related health, but these tests alone do not determine a specific cause or diagnosis.

title: Comprehensive metabolic panel
content: A comprehensive metabolic panel includes measurements related to metabolism, kidney and liver function, and electrolyte balance. Individual results should be interpreted together with the rest of the panel and clinical history.

title: Diabetes medicines and insulin
content: Diabetes medicines differ in how they work. Insulin is required in type 1 diabetes; treatment for type 2 diabetes depends on the individual's circumstances. A medication listed in a document does not confirm that it is currently taken. Discuss the medicine list with the treating clinician; this application does not select drugs, change treatment or recommend a dose.

title: High blood pressure and hypertension
content: Hypertension is high blood pressure and often has no symptoms. Evaluation uses blood-pressure measurements and clinical context. This educational background applies to an explicitly documented condition; laboratory results alone do not establish hypertension.

title: Chronic kidney disease
content: Chronic kidney disease involves kidney damage or reduced function over time. Blood and urine tests help evaluate kidney health. Diabetes and high blood pressure are relevant causes. An isolated abnormal creatinine result does not establish chronic kidney disease; duration and other clinical information matter.

title: Hypothyroidism
content: Hypothyroidism means the thyroid does not make enough thyroid hormone. Symptoms and blood testing inform assessment. A documented history should be reviewed with current results and clinical context; this application does not determine a thyroid medicine dose.

title: Anemia
content: Anemia concerns insufficient healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry oxygen adequately. Several causes are possible. Blood counts contribute to evaluation but a report alone does not determine the cause. This background is educational and does not independently confirm a diagnosis.

title: Type 1 diabetes: documented history and monitoring
content: Type 1 diabetes involves little or no insulin production. Glucose monitoring and clinician-directed insulin treatment are central to management. Blood glucose results alone do not determine diabetes type. Documented eye, kidney or nerve conditions should be reviewed in the clinical history rather than inferred from a simulated trajectory.

title: ADA 2026 section 6: assessment of glycemic status
passage: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics such as time in range
content: ADA recommendation 6.1 supports assessing glycemic status using A1C and/or CGM metrics, including time in range, above range and below range. Measured observations and model simulations must be distinguished: generated future values are not observed CGM evidence or a basis for medication changes.
